verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.6 (heading [D]): 'the gzip size of all JavaScript the route fetches before the reader's first interaction', table row 'each tool alone, on /tools/<id> | 90 kB'; SPEC.md 6.6: 'On a tool's own route (/tools/..., /embed/...) the keys are bare'; decisions/P6-A3.md '2026-10-25 P6-A3: the names of real forms, typeset at build time and loaded lazily'; DECISIONS.md 'MERGE: P6 stage 6.2, P6-A3' ('the typeset names load after the first action'). Together these support the finding's expected value.
verdicts.evidence: Read at f07eec6: SPEC 7.6 in full, 6.6 in full, 9.1 row 6, decisions/P6-A3.md, the MERGE entries on P6-A3 (stage 6.2, the review rulings, the repair), P6-size, reports/gate-G6.md sections 7 and 8 (report commit; it names gate commit f07eec6), and the known-and-decided list of P6-LENS-INSTRUCTIONS. Code at f07eec6: T13SatakeStudio.svelte's hydration $effect calls readLink(). When keyOf(next) !== keyOf(cfg), readLink calls setConfig(next), which ends with 'void loadNames().then(...)'. names.ts loadNames does import('./satakeNames'). The header of names.ts says the names load 'in the browser only after the reader's first change (loadNames), because the section weighs about 5 kB gzipped and SPEC 7.6 counts every script a route fetches before the first interaction'. P6-A3.md says the same: 'in the browser only after the reader's first change of decoration or of panel ... because the section weighs about 5 kB gzipped and the route measured 85.0 of its 90 kB without it'. P6-A3 sizes (repair): 87.0 kB of 90. MERGE recorded '85.0 kB of 90 (the typeset names load after the first action)'. So the builders' own records read 7.6 the way the finding does, and the hydration path for a link breaks their stated design. Possible counter-reading, checked: the 7.6 measuring bullet opens bare routes, and 'No tool may need it for its default state, so it never counts toward these limits' ties the worker exemption to the default state. This is an ambiguity, not a permitting sentence, because the exemption names only the worker script. Known-and-decided list: nothing on link states or T13's names. Gate G6 measured only bare routes (87.0 kB).
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because 7.6 counts all JavaScript fetched before the first interaction and exempts only the worker script. R2 fails because 6.6 places a link on the same route, and the builders' records (P6-A3, MERGE P6-A3, names.ts) read 7.6 as the finding does and promise the names only after the reader's first change, which hydration from a link contradicts; the bare-route method and the worker sentence's tie to the default state are an ambiguity for the owner, not a permission. R3 fails because T13 is phase 6 and G6 requires sizes on every page. R4 does not apply: the finding is not a mathematical value. R5 fails because the [D] of 7.6 sets the 90 kB limit, 92297 B lies outside it, and P6-A3 records the opposite behaviour. R6 fails because no record covers link-state sizes. Severity stays major ('a size budget exceeded').

verdicts.citation: R6: reports/gate-G6.md (report commit above f07eec6) section 8: '/glossary/ (a page with no tool, 83 typeset entries) measures 432.4 ms. Whether the same acceptance holds at G6, and for the glossary, is the owner's'; section 11, owner's part: '[ ] The lab item: whether the machine-bound acceptance of G3 holds for the 20 routes over at G6, /glossary/ included'; section 12. DECISIONS.md '2026-10-17 OWNER: gate G3's lab item accepted as machine-bound'. decisions/P3-X1.md, entries 'what the document tasks are (diagnosis)', 'the deeper render hint, measured, not adopted (request)' and 'remedy (b), KaTeX output, measured, route unchanged (request)'. P6-LENS-INSTRUCTIONS, 'Known and decided', lab timings item.
verdicts.evidence: Gate G6 already records this item as failed and open, page by page. Section 4 lists /glossary/, /sources/ and /atlas/C7/ among the 20 routes over on TBT, section 8 gives /glossary/ 432.4 ms, and section 11 hands the question to the owner. Section 12 says: 'lab (step 12): 20 routes over TBT; the item fails as measured. The red-team round's performance lens and the owner read section 8.' The mechanism the finding names has been on record since phase 3. P3-X1 found the TBT of static content to be 'the rendering of the content after the first view, not its parsing' (Style & Layout). It found that the deeper render hint 'gave TBT 0 ms ... because all the layout work moves into one task before the first paint, where TBT does not count it', and called that 'a choice for the owner'. It measured KaTeX's htmlAndMathml layers, noted that A-12 keeps MathML, and sent that request to the orchestrator. It also tried content-visibility and dropped it. The known-and-decided list says a lab number is a finding only as 'a regression, a wrong measurement method, or a repeatable figure well above that range'. The lens's own Lighthouse medians for /glossary/ are 66.1 and 26.7 ms (under 200), so it does not repeat the over-threshold figure. Gate G5 and earlier never measured /glossary/ in the lab, so no regression is measured. The lens also finds lab.mjs and its metric definitions correct. RT-07 lens section 6 requires 'a median of seven (Node) or five (browser) runs over the threshold on an otherwise idle machine'. The only over-threshold figure is the gate's median of 3, which the gate already reports.
verdicts.reason: the TBT of /glossary/ (and /sources/, /atlas/C7/) over 200 ms at G6 is already the gate's failing lab item, named and handed to the owner, and its mechanism is on record since decisions/P3-X1.md with its remedies left to the owner. The mechanism is the style and layout of server-rendered markup with KaTeX's two layers, counted only when it falls after the first paint. The lens adds diagnosis but no repeatable figure, no measured regression and no method error beyond those records.

The control (E7 node 7) also reaches 51 to 60 ms in some loads, so the test may fail now and then under CI load'. round-p5/out/TALLY.md line 92 (MERGE): 'Confirmer's note: the adopted link-task test is marginal for C8 node 7 at load 1'. reports/gate-G6.md sections 4 and 12: the failure of T12.spec.ts:1242 is recorded as open, with its next step. verdicts.evidence: The finding's cause is that T12.spec.ts:1242 times T12's own Svelte hydration plus the node's facts. That task straddles 50 ms for case and control alike, so the test fails under load without a regression. The P5 confirmer recorded exactly this when the test was adopted: profile, control at 51 to 60 ms, and 'may fail now and then under CI load'. MERGE carried the note into the round's tally when it merged the fix. Gate G6 reports the failure of this exact test ([0, 53, 56], median 53; it passed at the CI base with [0, 0, 51]) as a failing row and a tracked open item. For T12's long-task tests in general, MERGE recorded that 7.6 bounds engine calls only, that the tests ask more, and that the residual is Svelte work, with the choice left to the owner. Read at f07eec6: T12.spec.ts:1195-1255. The test maps a hydration task under 50 ms to 0 and asserts median(big) <= max(50, median(control) + 15), which is what the records describe. The finding also says that G6's failure has no phase 6 cause. That contradicts the gate's 'Next' line in section 12 and is a note for the owner, not a separate defect. The finding's own specRef and observed cite the confirm record.
verdicts.reason: the weakness the finding names was recorded by the phase 5 confirmer and noted by MERGE when the test was adopted, and the test's G6 failure is an open, tracked item of gate-G6.md. The weakness is a link-hydration test that times T12's own Svelte hydration, so case and control both straddle 50 ms and the test fails under load without a regression. T12's long-task tests that time Svelte work stay as written pending the owner's choice. The new diagnosis (no phase 6 cause) corrects the gate's 'Next' line and belongs to the owner as a note.

verdicts.citation: R2: SPEC.md 5.6, last sentence: 'A tool decides whether a board is of finite type by calling `classify` once when the board is loaded, never by running an enumeration into its cap.' SPEC.md 5.1 E-11: 'The engine adds the checks of section 5.6. The test for finite type is classify, whose verdict is kept in a WeakMap from board objects to verdicts inside the engine module'. SPEC.md 5.1 E-5: 'no hidden state, apart from the cache of E-11'. CONTRACTS.md 2.4, phase 6: 'satakeRecord(name: string, entry: SatakeCatalogueEntry): SatakeRecord'. RT-07 lens attack 24: 'count classify calls on a board change with a wrapper around the engine export'. DECISIONS.md 'RT-FIX-P5-t12-perf: one board object per name in T12': '5.6 says once when the board is loaded and E-11 keeps the verdict per board object; neither says how a tool ... keeps the object'.
verdicts.evidence: The finding counts classifyUncached computations. By its own stacks they come from three places: state.ts:174 verdictOf (the site layer's call of the exported classify, on resolveBoard's object), satake.ts:171 guard (on T13's boardOf object) and satakeCatalogue.ts:271 guard (on the board satakeRecord builds). At f07eec6 both guards are engine guards: satake.ts imports requireFinite from guards.ts, and requireFinite calls cachedClassify (guards.ts:58-59). They do not call the exported classify, which a wrapper around the export (attack 24's method) would count. So on a load the tool path calls classify once (state.ts:174), and the other computations are the E-11 checks that 5.6's table requires of the Satake functions ('throw NotFiniteType'). One of them is unavoidable under the contract. satakeRecord takes a name (CONTRACTS 2.4), so it must build boardFromName(name) and guard it (P6-A2 'the order of checks' records exactly this). E-5 forbids the engine a per-name store of boards beside E-11's cache, so each call classifies a new object. If 5.6 counted engine guard computations, CONTRACTS 2.4, E-5 and E-11 would make 'once' impossible for T13, which must show catalogue records. The P5 precedent (P5-RT-07-02) differs: there all three computations were the tool's own verdictOf calls, one per resolveBoard in three tasks. The finding gives the cost of each extra classify as 0.07 to 0.14 ms.
verdicts.reason: the finding counts the wrong quantity. 5.6 bounds the tool's calls of classify when a board loads, and T13's path calls it once per load (state.ts:174). The extra computations are E-11's guards inside satake and satakeRecord, which 5.6's table and E-11 require. One of them follows from satakeRecord's name-based signature (CONTRACTS 2.4) and E-5's ban on hidden state. Attack 24 of the lens counts calls of the engine export, not guard computations.
